about.title: Escalon Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Escalon is a small town of about 7,523 people, and when a life is lost here it is felt across the whole community, not just one household. In 2025, public records counted 17 injury collisions in Escalon, 23 people hurt, and one traffic death. Behind that single number is a family in San Joaquin County trying to work out what happens next. Traffic along Route 120, McHenry Avenue, Escalon Avenue and Main Street accounts for much of the local collision activity, with reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, separate from any criminal case, brought by the people California law names first: a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. It can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive connects Escalon families with an independent attorney at no cost, and that attorney works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Escalon Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected promptly keeps those dates from slipping by while you grieve.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorney you are matched with works on contingency, so your family does not pay legal fees out of pocket.

items.question: My loved one died in a crash on Route 120 near Escalon. Does that change the deadline?
items.answer: It might. Route 120 is a state highway, and if any part of your claim involves a public agency, such as a road design or maintenance issue, California requires a government claim to be filed much sooner than the usual two-year deadline. An attorney can review the collision report and tell you quickly whether a government entity may be involved.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs separately from any criminal prosecution in San Joaquin County. Your family does not need a conviction to bring a claim, and the two cases move on their own timelines.

items.question: What losses can a wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Every family's situation is different, and an independent attorney can walk through what applies to yours. Nothing about the outcome can be promised, but you can get an honest assessment for free.
